evidence: Pre-fix src/config.js resolveSecrets did `if (!value) throw` for every preset with no credentialOptional awareness, while the flag lived only on PROVIDERS.local, so `preset: local` could never omit its key. Commit 0518628 moved credentialOptional onto PRESETS.local and threaded `optional` into resolveSecrets (`if (!value && !optional)`), which is the reviewer's first option with the column placed where both paths read it, plus tests on the config path.
guidance_note: When a table row gains a capability column, list every consumer of the table it hangs off (here PRESETS feeds both synthesizeProviderConfig and config.js resolveSecrets) and put the column on the table both consumers read, with a test per consumer.

evidence: The new `credential || ''` path makes `core.setSecret('')` the default for a keyless local run, so registering an empty mask is real; the reviewer's claim that some runners then redact all later output is not supported by anything in the packet. Instead of the suggested call-site guard, the agent routed both setSecret sites through one `credentialsToMask(...).filter(Boolean)` seam, which also covers the config-file path that the guard would have missed now that it too yields ''.
guidance_note: When a change makes a new value ('' credential) flow into existing effect sites, grep every consumer of that field (both core.setSecret calls) in the original PR and decide the empty case at each one.

evidence: The PR adds a PROVIDER value and three action inputs but bumped 1.57.1 → 1.57.2; the agent confirms CONTRIBUTING.md:59 picks the level by consumer-contract change and that the patch level came from a mechanical 'make version-bump green' step. 0518628 sets 1.58.0.
guidance_note: Pick the semver level from CONTRIBUTING.md's consumer-contract rule when bumping, not from whatever turns check-version-bump.sh green; a new input or enum value is a minor bump.

evidence: No shipped preset combines oauth with credentialOptional (reviewer concedes 'nothing breaks yet'), so this is a load-time invariant gap rather than a live bug; the cheap guard beside the existing oauth/pinned check fits the table's 'validated once' design. The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive for causation: 0518628 relocated the boolean check from assertProvidersSafe to assertPresetsSafe nearly verbatim, and the missing oauth cross-check was equally absent from the pre-review provider-row version.
guidance_note: When adding a column to a table that already has a cross-column safety check (oauth requires pinned), check the new column against every existing column it can contradict and add the refusal in the same commit.

evidence: The reviewer's 'unverified anywhere' was wrong: the agent's issue comment at 06:43, before this 06:47 round, shows opencode-ai@1.17.9 accepting `"apiKey": ""` against Ollama with LOCAL_API_KEY unset. The missing unit test was a real gap, and 572d2a6 added one asserting the serialized config keeps apiKey ''. The flag is a false positive: the anchored line `credential: { kind: preset.credentialKind, value: credential || '' }` in resolveEndpoint is from the original PR, not 0518628.
guidance_note: When a behaviour is verified live against an external tool, pin the observed contract (here the serialized `apiKey: ""`) in a unit test in the same PR so the evidence is in the diff, not only in a PR comment.

evidence: 0518628 (the F1 fix) added the credential-optional exception to the README's validation paragraph, and the F1 reply claims the README was updated because the fix made 'an unset credentialEnv always fails the run' untrue. But the Secrets section's 'Every `credentialEnv` reachable in the chain must be set and non-empty at startup, or the run fails fast' was left unchanged until 572d2a6. The README stated one rule in two places and the fix updated only one.
guidance_note: When a fix makes a documented rule false, grep the docs for every restatement of that rule (here 'credentialEnv' + 'unset'/'fails') and update all of them in the same commit.

evidence: The Inputs table's PROVIDER row omitting `local` is an original-PR gap. It was reported in both the round 0 and round 1 summaries under 'Findings outside the reviewed diff' (README.md:102) and went unaddressed until it came back inline in round 2, so the ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT 572d2a6 flag is a false positive: 572d2a6 touched only the Secrets sentence, and line 102 had not changed since the PR opened.
guidance_note: When adding an enum value, grep the repo for an existing member list (e.g. 'claude-subscription') and update every enumeration; and treat a review summary's 'outside the reviewed diff' findings as findings to address, since they have no thread to remind you.

narrative: The PR added a `local` provider with an optional credential. Round 0 found real gaps: the optional-credential property held only on the PROVIDER path (F1), an empty string was masked (F2), and the semver level was wrong (F3). The agent fixed F1 well by moving the column onto the preset, but missed a second README restatement of the credential rule, which produced F6. The agent also ignored the out-of-diff README:102 finding in two consecutive round summaries. Only that finding, F7, drove round 2, so round 2 (and the approval round after it) would not have been needed if the round-0 summary item had been fixed with the first batch. F4 and F5 were new findings on original or relocated code, not fallout from fixes.
guidance_observations: The agent addressed only inline threads and skipped the 'Findings outside the reviewed diff' list in the review summary twice, which cost a full review round for a one-word README fix.

Fix replies claimed doc updates were complete ('so it now names the exception') without grepping for other restatements of the same rule. A grep for the rule's key phrase before replying would have closed F6 in the first fix.
The agent did the live opencode verification before round 1 but did not pin it in a test until the reviewer asked; keeping verification in the diff would have pre-empted F5.
